title: File:Upper Falls (Old Man's Cave Gorge, Hocking Hills, Ohio, USA) 2 (34835868936).jpg
author: James St. John
description: This waterfalls forms the head of Old Man's Cave Gorge in the scenic Hocking Hills of southeastern Ohio.  This is the second, or middle tier/drop with a plunge pool at the bottom of the photo.  The rocks are sandstones to pebbly sandstones of the Lower Mississippian Black Hand Sandstone, traditionally interpreted as an ancient delta deposit.  Modern work has shown it is an incised valley fill complex.

title: File:Devil's Bathtub (Old Man's Cave Gorge, Hocking Hills, Ohio, USA) 4 (34877112325).jpg
author: James St. John
description:
This distinctively shaped plunge pool occurs at the base of a small waterfalls in Old Man's Cave Gorge in the scenic Hocking Hills of southeastern Ohio.  It appears to be a composite pothole-plunge pool.  Potholes form as high-energy water swirls abrasive sediments (sand to gravel) in depressions, causing them to deepen and widen.

The rocks are part of the Lower Mississippian Black Hand Sandstone.  This unit was traditionally interpreted as an ancient delta deposit, but modern work has shown it is an incised valley fill complex.
